answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Mirror Rule. At each epoch boundary the agent must reproduce a cipher-derived challenge using its own past interaction history; the verifier compares this against a mirror of the prior epoch's behaviour. Consistency across epochs is the admission signal. A clone fleet cannot fake it because each identity's history is unique: copying another identity's responses fails the challenge, and fabricating history costs one full epoch of genuine interactions per clone before it can even attempt entry.
